props.title: For Y'ur Height Only

sections.content: The Filipino exploitation film For Y'ur Height Only stands as one of the most delightfully bizarre entries in spy cinema, starring 2'9" actor Weng Weng as Agent 00. This James Bond parody blazed a unique trail through action cinema, combining martial arts, espionage tropes, and outlandish stunts that made creative use of Weng Weng's small stature. The film belongs to a fascinating wave of Filipino exploitation cinema of the 1970s-80s, alongside works like The One Armed Executioner (1983) and They Call Her Cleopatra Wong (1978), which remixed popular Western genres with distinctly Filipino flair.

sections.content: The film's impact rippled through cult cinema circles, inspiring a wave of unconventional action heroes. While Hollywood had The Spy Who Loved Me (1977) and Moonraker (1979), Filipino cinema countered with this uniquely subversive take that challenged action hero physical stereotypes. Director Eddie Nicart's clever use of camera angles and practical effects created convincing action sequences that made Weng Weng appear formidable despite his size, influencing later films like Time Chasers (1994) in showing how creativity could overcome budget limitations. SUBHEAD: The Rise of Filipino Exploitation Cinema

The success of For Y'ur Height Only came during the golden age of Filipino exploitation films, when directors like Eddie Nicart and Bobby A. Suarez were churning out genre-bending features that found international audiences. This era produced gems like Wonder Women (1973) and Black Mama, White Mama (1973), mixing Western action tropes with distinctly Filipino storytelling sensibilities. The period represented a unique moment when Filipino filmmakers could experiment freely, resulting in these gloriously eccentric productions that continue to influence cult cinema.
